overview: The Medford School Committee is responsible for the district's budget, facility planning, and educational policies, currently managing a transition in permanent leadership and a massive high school reconstruction project. Since 2024, the body has navigated significant fiscal challenges, including the allocation of voter-approved override funds and the restoration of staff positions. The committee also manages chronic elementary school overcrowding through facility utilization studies and classroom relocations. As of late 2026, the body is focused on developing a community-informed strategic plan and finalizing the schematic designs for the new Medford Comprehensive High School.

threads.name: High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a multi-year effort to rebuild Medford High School, starting with the approval of CTE program expansions and the co-location of the Curtis-Tufts program for MSBA consideration. After completing the eligibility phase and reaching an enrollment agreement for 1,395 students, the body selected an Owner's Project Manager and a designer to lead a feasibility study. Site selection narrowed the focus to the existing campus, excluding sites like Medford Square due to size constraints and 999-year deed restrictions. By 2026, the committee was reviewing six design options and adjusting educational plans to maximize MSBA reimbursement and building efficiency.

threads.name: Elementary Overcrowding and Space Utilization
threads.summary: The district faced a persistent capacity crisis at Roberts Elementary School, where enrollment surpassed 590 students, leading to calls for redistricting and space planning. To address immediate needs, the committee voted to relocate preschool classrooms from the Roberts to other elementary sites and formed a strategic space planning task force. The body explored restructuring the district into K-4 and 5-8 grade spans but ultimately delayed any major middle school configuration changes until at least 2028. Currently, the committee is refining a formal policy to regulate intra-district school reassignment requests based on enrollment buffers.

threads.name: District Leadership and Superintendent Search
threads.summary: Following the departure of Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent in early 2025, the committee conducted a search for interim leadership to ensure continuity during major facility projects. Dr. Suzanne Galusi was appointed as Interim Superintendent and subsequently underwent a formal evaluation and induction program. After reviewing transition findings and considering the potential disruption of an external search, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent. A three-year contract for the new superintendent was finalized and approved in May 2026.

threads.name: HVAC Replacement and Capital Repairs
threads.summary: The committee prioritized major infrastructure upgrades, beginning with the authorization of $25.7 million in bonds for comprehensive HVAC replacements and roof refurbishments at the McGlynn and Andrews schools. A facilities condition assessment identified over $83 million in necessary repairs across the district, leading to a prioritized multi-year capital plan. This included the approval of a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roof replacement at Roberts Elementary. Smaller projects included skylight repairs at the McGlynn and hot water heater replacements at the Brooks School.

threads.name: Vocational (CTE) Program Management
threads.summary: Career and Technical Education programs saw significant expansion efforts, including requests for new plumbing and veterinary science pathways. To manage oversubscribed programs fairly, the committee adopted a new lottery-based admissions policy to replace previous weighted systems. The body also approved an honors pilot program for juniors and seniors to earn advanced credit through co-op employment or capstone projects. Regular viability forms were updated for the MSBA to reflect current vocational enrollment and waitlist data.

threads.name: After-School and Summer Program Capacity
threads.summary: The district struggled with significant waitlists for before- and after-school care, prompting reports on transportation hurdles and staffing constraints. Following a consultancy with the Belmont Afterschool Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC), the committee approved a plan to increase capacity by 150 seats and transition to a model with full-time site directors. New tuition rate cards were established to fund these expansions while offering more flexible multi-day options. By late 2026, the administration reported a 68% reduction in the after-school program waitlist.

threads.name: Graduation Requirements and Academic Accountability
threads.summary: In response to state ballot initiatives and updated regulations, the committee revised Policy IKF to remove MCAS as a graduation requirement, replacing it with successful completion of aligned coursework. The body also updated health and physical education requirements to allow for more elective flexibility and independent study. In 2026, the committee approved a pilot for late-entry testing schedules at the high school and received accountability reports showing that seven out of eight schools had improved their state percentiles. New policies were also adopted to regulate the use of generative AI in schools and prohibit its use for qualitative grading by educators.
